proposals.hypothesis: LiAlSiO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium aluminosilicate built from fully oxidized Al3+, Si4+ and O2- with no reducible transition metal. Its Li-stuffed tetrahedral framework should resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2 and is generally tolerant of the sulfide Li6PS5Cl, so it is a plausible insulating interlayer.
proposals.motivation: The earlier LiAlSiO4 proposal (mp-aaaaajjj) was a wide-gap, fully oxidized silicate coating, and this polymorph-level candidate tests the same composition from the available list.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating phosphate that is chemically compatible with both LiCoO2 and the sulfide Li6PS5Cl. Its P-O bonding should resist oxidation at 4.0 V and limit interfacial sulfide decomposition, so it is a strong baseline coating candidate for the cathode-electrolyte interface.

Li4P2O7 is a Li-rich, wide-gap pyrophosphate with the same P-O polyanion chemistry as the Li3PO4 baseline. Its high Li content and fully oxidized P5+ should resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2 and limit reactivity with the sulfide Li6PS5Cl, so it is a close analog for coating refinement.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was evaluated as a phosphate baseline coating with good expected compatibility, so a closely related Li-rich phosphate is the natural refinement step.

proposal.hypothesis: Li2O is a Li-rich, wide-gap oxide (band gap well above 2 eV) built from fully oxidized O2- and Li+ with no reducible transition metal. It should resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2 and is thermodynamically stable against the sulfide Li6PS5Cl. It is a different chemical family from the phosphate baseline, so it tests whether a simple oxide coating also limits interfacial decomposition.
proposal.motivation: Li3PO4 (mp-aaaaaegs) was a wide-gap, Li-rich, oxidation-resistant baseline, and Li2O shares that Li-rich, fully oxidized oxide character while lying outside the phosphate family.

proposal.hypothesis: LiF is a very wide-gap, electronically insulating, Li-rich fluoride. Its Li-F bonding is extremely resistant to oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2 and it is thermodynamically inert toward the sulfide Li6PS5Cl. A fluoride coating is a chemically distinct family from the earlier phosphate and simple-oxide choices, so it tests whether an inert halide interlayer suppresses interfacial decomposition.
proposal.motivation: Earlier wide-gap, Li-rich, oxidation-resistant coatings (Li3PO4 and Li2O) were evaluated as baselines, and LiF extends that Li-rich, fully oxidized, insulating character into the fluoride family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li8ZrO6 is a very Li-rich orthozirconate built from fully oxidized Zr4+ and O2-, with no reducible transition metal. Its high Li2O content and wide gap should resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2, and oxide-rich Li compounds are generally thermodynamically tolerant of Li6PS5Cl. It extends the Li-rich oxide character of the earlier Li2O and Li3PO4 baselines into a Zr-based composition.
proposal.motivation: Li2O (mp-aaaaacxk) was proposed as a wide-gap, Li-rich, fully oxidized oxide coating, and Li8ZrO6 shares that Li2O-rich character while adding a Zr4+ framework that should be electrochemically inert.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3BO3 is a Li-rich, fully oxidized orthoborate with B3+ and O2- only, so it has no reducible or easily oxidized cation and should be wide-gap and electronically insulating. Its high Li content and oxidation resistance should suit LiCoO2 at 4.0 V, and its Li-O bonding is expected to be thermodynamically tolerant toward Li6PS5Cl. It moves to the borate family, which has not yet been tested, while staying in the Li-rich oxide character of the earlier baselines.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li-rich, wide-gap, oxidation-resistant oxide and phosphate coatings (Li3PO4, Li2O) were proposed as baselines, and Li3BO3 extends that fully oxidized, Li-rich oxide character into a new borate family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li8SiO6 is a Li-rich orthosilicate built from fully oxidized Si4+ and O2- with no reducible transition metal. Its high Li2O content and wide gap should resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2, and Li-O-rich oxides are generally tolerant of the sulfide Li6PS5Cl. It is a silicate-family coating that tests whether a Li2O-rich oxide with a tetravalent non-transition-metal center suppresses interfacial decomposition.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li-rich, fully oxidized oxide coatings (Li2O and the Li8ZrO6 refinement) were proposed as wide-gap, oxidation-resistant interlayers, and Li8SiO6 carries that Li2O-rich character into the silicate family.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlSiO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium aluminosilicate built from fully oxidized Al3+, Si4+ and O2- with no reducible transition metal. Its Li-stuffed tetrahedral framework should resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2 and is generally tolerant of the sulfide Li6PS5Cl, so it is a plausible interlayer. It stays in the silicate family of the Li8SiO6 proposal while adding a trivalent Al3+ framework cation.
proposal.motivation: Li8SiO6 (mp-aaabqgb-family silicate proposal) was an Li-rich, fully oxidized silicate coating candidate, and LiAlSiO4 keeps that silicate character with a more stable, lower-Li framework.

proposal.hypothesis: Li6Zr2O7 is a Li-rich zirconate built from fully oxidized Zr4+ and O2-, with no reducible transition metal. Its high Li2O content and wide gap should resist oxidation at 4.0 V against LiCoO2, and Li-O-rich oxides are generally tolerant of the sulfide Li6PS5Cl. It is the closest available analog to the proposed Li8ZrO6 zirconate, so it tests the Li-rich Zr-oxide coating concept.
